title: Settlement 3: Function and Hierarchy
subject: Geography
description: Settlement functions, Peel as a case study, and how settlements change as you go up the settlement hierarchy.
author: L.M.

cards.front: Market town
cards.back: For trading goods brought in from the surrounding areas

cards.front: Industrial settlement
cards.back:
Has many factories

(Such as a steelworks or shipbuilding.)

cards.front: Tourist resort
cards.back: Aimed at people travelling to the area

cards.front: Mining settlement
cards.back: Built around a mine

cards.front: Administrative settlement
cards.back: Contains government or council buildings, or many offices

cards.front: Port
cards.back: For fishing, trade or transport

cards.front: Residential settlement
cards.back: Housing for commuters

cards.front: What was Peel originally?
cards.back:
A market town

(Fishermen, farmers and other producers brought goods to sell in the market square. It was also an important port.)

cards.front: What is Peel focused on nowadays?
cards.back:
Tourism

(It also has lots of residential housing and a port.)

cards.front: Why does Peel have lots of residential housing?
cards.back: For people who commute to other parts of the island for work

cards.front: What does 'commute' mean?
cards.back: Travel to work

cards.front: What kind of port does Peel have now?
cards.back: A marina

cards.front: List the settlement hierarchy from smallest to largest.
cards.back: Isolated dwelling, hamlet, village, town, city, capital

cards.front: What is at the top of the settlement hierarchy?
cards.back: Capital

cards.front: What is at the bottom of the settlement hierarchy?
cards.back: Isolated dwelling

cards.front: What comes between hamlet and town in the hierarchy?
cards.back: Village

cards.front: What comes between town and capital in the hierarchy?
cards.back: City

cards.front: Settlement hierarchy: what happens to size (area) as you go up?
cards.back: It increases

cards.front: Settlement hierarchy: what happens to population as you go up?
cards.back: It increases

cards.front: Settlement hierarchy: what happens to the distance between settlements as you go up?
cards.back:
It increases

(Because settlements start competing with others.)

cards.front: Settlement hierarchy: what happens to shops as you go up?
cards.back:
The number and size of shops increase

(There are also likely to be more global brands.)

cards.front: Settlement hierarchy: what happens to services as you go up?
cards.back:
The number and size of services increase

(Schools, hospitals and sports centres. A larger population needs more of these.)

cards.front: Settlement hierarchy: what happens to the number of settlements as you go up?
cards.back:
It decreases

(There should be more villages in a country than there are cities.)

questions.question: Which settlement function means 'built around a mine'?
questions.explanation: A mining settlement is built around a mine.

questions.question: A settlement with many factories, such as a steelworks, is...
questions.explanation: Industrial settlements have many factories, such as steelworks or shipbuilding.

questions.question: What is Peel mostly focused on nowadays?
questions.explanation: Peel was originally a market town and port, but now focuses a lot on tourism.

questions.question: Which comes between hamlet and town in the settlement hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Isolated dwelling, hamlet, village, town, city, capital.

questions.question: Which DECREASES as you go up the settlement hierarchy?
questions.explanation: The number of settlements decreases: there are more villages in a country than cities. The others increase.

questions.question: Why do services increase as you go up the hierarchy?
options: A larger population needs more of them
questions.explanation: A larger population needs more schools, hospitals and sports centres.
